715273.title: A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z
715273.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have four customers with open invoices on today's date, named "10 Trucking" (customer A), "2 Trucking" (customer B), "A-1 Towing" (customer C) and "a1 towing" (customer D). Their names differ by a number, a dash or capitals.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
715273.custom_steps:
1. Look at the header of the customer name column (the first column).
  2. Without clicking any column header, find the four customers in the list (scroll down until they load if they are further down).
715273.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The customer name column (the first column) is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Step 2:

  • All four customers are listed, reading from top to bottom customer A, then customer B, then customer C, then customer D (other customers may sit between them).
  • "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" because names compare character by character.
  • "A-1 Towing" comes before "a1 towing" because capitals are ignored and the dash compares as a character.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R1: “A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z; A/P Summary opens with vendors in name order, A to Z.”
  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing". Names that start with a punctuation mark follow the same order: "#1 Diesel", "-1 Diesel", "10 Trucking", "@Home Towing".”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-summary-date-only.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary as it opens today" (Production (before)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting" (today's look, for comparison only)

715277.title: Two customer names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere
715277.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have two customers with open invoices on today's date, whose names differ only in capitals: customer A and customer B.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
715277.custom_steps:
1. Find customer A and customer B in the list and note which one is higher.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu at the right of the title.
  3. Open the PDF and find the two names.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and find the two names.
  6. Reload the page and find the two names again.
715277.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The two customers sit next to each other (no other customer between them) in one order.

Step 2:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 3:

  • The two names are in the same order as on screen.

Step 4:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 5:

  • The two rows are in the same order as on screen.

Step 6:

  • After the reload they are still in the same order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV.   3. Keep scrolling into customer B's rows.

  6. Scroll fast back up through customer B's and customer A's rows.

  • Customer B's row pushes customer A's row up and off and takes its place.
  • Only one group row is pinned at a time.

Step 3:

  • Customer B's row stays pinned.

Step 4:

  • The change reverses: customer A's row comes back down into the pinned place.

Step 5:

  • At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

  • Two group rows never overlap.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S5-R7: “Choosing locations narrows every row, group, subtotal, total, page count, sort and export to the open documents at those locations. A row belongs to the location of its own document. On A/P: a bill belongs to the location of the delivery it was received on; a vendor credit from a vendor return belongs to that return's location; any other vendor credit keeps its vendor's location, as today. 715456.title: A/R Summary: the Totals row adds up exactly the rows each filter leaves
715456.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and location B, with location A's name first in A to Z order.
  • Have three new customers (created for this test) with only these open documents on today's date:
  • Customer A: an invoice of $1,000.00 at location A 15 days past due, an invoice of $400.00 at location B 45 days past due and an unused credit memo of $150.00 at location A.
  • Customer B: an invoice of $700.00 at location A 45 days past due and an invoice of $250.00 at location B 100 days past due.
  • Customer C: an invoice of $900.00 at location A 5 days past due.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
715456.custom_steps:
1. In the Customer filter, tick customer A and customer B.
  2. In the Location filter, untick location B.
  3. In the Location menu, click "Select all".
  4. In the Past due filter, tick "91+ days".
  5. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  6. Open the PDF and read its Totals row.
  7. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  8. Open the CSV and read its Totals row.
715456.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Two rows remain.
  • Customer C is gone.
  • Customer A appears once, with Location "Multiple" and a Total of $1,250.00 (1,000.00 + 400.00 − 150.00).
  • Customer B's Total is $950.00 (700.00 + 250.00).
  • The Totals row's Total is $2,200.00 (1,250.00 + 950.00).

Step 2:

  • The report narrows to location A: customer A's Total is $850.00 (1,000.00 − 150.00, its location A documents only).
  • Customer B's is $700.00.
  • The Totals row's Total is $1,550.00.

Step 3:

  • Every location is ticked again.

Step 4:

  • The chip reads "Past due: 91+ days".
  • Only customer B is listed (customer A has nothing more than 90 days past due), at its full balance: 31-60 Days $700.00, 91 And Over $250.00, Total $950.00.
  • The Totals row's Total is $950.00.

Step 5:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 6:

  • The PDF's Totals row reads $950.00 for the Total, the same as the screen.

Step 7:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 8:

  • The CSV's Totals row reads $950.00 for the Total, the same as the screen.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
  • S5-R8: “On the Summaries, a customer's or vendor's row adds up only their open documents at the chosen locations; a customer or vendor with nothing open there is not listed.”
  • S5-R17: “With ranges ticked, A/R Summary and A/P Summary list only the customers or vendors with some open invoice or bill amount in a ticked range; their rows show their full balances in every bucket.”
  • S6-R4: “On A/R Summary and A/P Summary a row shows the location's name when all of that customer's or vendor's open documents at the chosen locations are at one location, otherwise "Multiple".”
  • Key Decisions, row location: “A row belongs to the location of its own open document (the invoice, credit memo or deposit; the bill or vendor credit), the same location the Location column shows. Rationale: the aging reports list open documents, not payments, so a partly paid invoice keeps its own location and the filter never contradicts the column. Rejected: splitting a balance by where each payment was taken.”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html); page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p7-past-due-ticked.png: figure "Past due ticked" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p4-summaries-show-multiple.png: figure "Summaries show "Multiple"" (This build (after)), board "4. Location filter and Location column"
  • ar-ap-p7-call-list-on-a-r-collection.png: figure "Call list on A/R Collection" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"

The design's own words:

  • "31-60 days and 91+ days ticked: the chip reads "Past due: 2 ranges" in blue. The Summary lists only customers with an amount in those ranges, at full balances; the Totals row adds up exactly these rows. S5-R15, S5-R16, S5-R17, S5-R18, S5-R19." (caption of "Past due ticked")
  • "A customer with open documents at two locations reads "Multiple"; sorted by Location here. S6-R4, S6-R5, S5-R8." (caption of "Summaries show "Multiple"")
  • "Customer picked: the group row shows "Phone:" and, for users with View and Manage AP/AR Data, "Credit term:". The Totals row follows the customer filter. S9-R1, S9-R2, S5-R18. Exports carry the same lines and columns: S9-R3, S3-R5, S3-R8a." (caption of "Call list on A/R Collection")

715485.title: Design: A/R Detail in dark theme: chips, links and Totals row readable
715485.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location column shows.
  • Have a customer with a long name (more than 40 characters) and open documents at both locations on today's date, including a credit memo, so the page shows a long name and a credit memo row, which must not overlap or be cut off.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, in dark theme at 100% zoom.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with every group expanded (Expand all).
  • Open Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) in a second tab, also in dark theme, for comparison.
715485.custom_steps:
1. Look at the title row and the filter row.
  2. Look at the chips in their resting state.
  3. Look at the document numbers that are links.
  4. Look at the "Open Balance" column and the Totals row, and compare with Sales By Customer.
  5. Press Tab until a link has keyboard focus.
  6. Look across the whole page for any text that overlaps, is cut off, or is hard to read on the dark background.
715485.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The title, info icon and ⋯ on one line, the filter row below, as in light theme.

Step 2:

  • "Customer: All customers" and "Past due: Any" show in the resting (grey) style and are readable.

Step 3:

  • They are blue, semi-bold and not underlined, and readable on the dark background.

Step 4:

  • "Open Balance" pinned right and bold on the header, rows and Totals row.
  • Side by side, the Totals row looks the same as Sales By Customer's in dark theme: the same background colour, text size and weight.

Step 5:

  • The focused link is underlined.

Step 6:

  • Nothing overlaps, is cut off or is hard to read.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11537 (Story 7, Document links open where they can), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S7-R7: “Links use the native report link style (the same blue as Work In Progress, semi-bold, no underline, underlined only on keyboard focus), readable in light and dark theme.”
  • S8-R3: “The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer. Narrower than 1440 pixels, the table scrolls sideways under the pinned column.”
  • S8-R4: “The Totals row uses the native totals row style of the newer reports.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked.
